sample_a.reason: More weight remains undefined. The example repeats the frequency claim but never shows what is counted, how a result score changes or why a different result would move up. The text-poster composition provides no missing explanation.

sample_b.teaches: Across six files, plan appears five times and pension twice. Giving plan matches one point and pension matches three moves Pension limits from an equal-score tie to above the four plan-only results.
sample_b.reason: The mechanism is sufficient and the point arithmetic is visible. The remaining concerns are the same phone-scale small text and visual-brief mismatch described for the candidate. No minimum number of findings or predetermined rejection was used.

explain_back: This is a collection-relative way to score matches. A plan match separates almost none of the six files, while pension selects a smaller set. In this method pension therefore contributes 3 points and plan contributes 1. Matching both scores 4. Pension limits rises from a tie on 1 point with four plan-only files to 3 points above their 1. The common term is retained. Higher score is neither proof of truth nor guaranteed relevance.
transfer: If plan appears in 2 of 6 and pension in 5 of 6, the method reverses their contributions: plan receives 3 and pension 1. A file matching both still scores 4; a plan-only file scores 3 and a pension-only file 1. The original six named files cannot retain their original match patterns while those frequencies reverse; this is a changed collection. It is rarity within that collection, not the word pension itself, that receives the higher weight.
